text.p: The Turkish lira eased to 92,415 against the dollar on Thursday from 92,075 at Wednesday's close on a higher dollar/mark and banks' dollar demand.
The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers at 92,275 lira at the opening, up from 91,950 at Wednesday's close. It further raised the rate to 92,300 lira.
Bankers said the banks' dollar demand was relatively high due to expectations of a higher inflation rate in the last four months of the year. September inflation data are due on Friday.
O/n money traded between 72 and 75 percent, and the central bank injected 14.2 trillion lira at 75 percent on the afternoon.
The central bank had injected 12.6 trillion lira by overnight lending at 75 percent on Wednesday.
T-bill yields rose slightly on lower liquidity. Bankers said the yields firmed up to one point on sales from some banks at the opening, but eased slightly later.
The average yield on the most heavily traded May 7 paper firmed to 129.09 percent from 128.67 on Wednesday.
The second most active March 26 paper yielded 126.58 percent average, up from Wednesday's 126.31 average.
